ms.report:
What we Promised:
Orcfax will produce a qualitative research report which evaluates current L2 protocols and tools available to Cardano projects With the hope of using this to inform proof-of-concept development. This research and its findings were to be published on our public Orcfax GitHub repository.

What we delivered:
Orcfax has conducted limited research which investigates a sample set of consensus protocols, and this can be found within our public GitHub repository. This research was executed with a limited initial understanding of the consensus landscape, but covers topics such as: what might be Orcfax requirements for staking? What consensus resources exist for Cardano developers? How do these resources map to Orcfax requirements?

It is our hope that this exercise will inform future development by Orcfax.

Abstract
This paper provides a brief comparison of various consensus protocols which were
assessed against an initial understanding of consensus requirements and
identified validator roles for the decentralized validator network, EchoNet. The
purpose being for Orcfax to ascertain whether an existing consensus protocol, as
a drop in solution for Orcfax, adequately meets its needs for: high throughput,
low latency, fault tolerance, and scalability in a multi-validator environment.
Based on the analysis of each consensus protocol and the initial Must Have
requirements identified by Orcfax, none of the reviewed consensus protocols
fully meets the needs of EchoNet. However, the most interesting line for
additional inquiry is CometBFT which aligned with several of the core Orcfax
requirements for a consensus protocol.

The other consensus protocols examined in this paper were: Hydra, Hydrozoa,
Iagon, Lodestar, Midgard, NEM, Raft, Snowball, CometBFT, and VeChainThor. Each
was assessed for its efficiency, reliability, scalability, as well as its
capacity to support a decentralized, real-time data validation network.

ms.report:
The specific comments associated with the last rejection were not visible to our team as feedback is not released until all reviewers have submitted. Our team reviewed the submission and found several areas to add clarifying language; to avoid asking reviewers to infer how the repository satisfies the approved criteria, we have revised the submission and added a direct requirement-to-evidence mapping.
The public repo can be found here: https://github.com/orcfax/melon
The approved milestone requires proof-of-concept software demonstrating that a validator node operator can:
・receive external source data;
・apply validation logic;
・compare its result with other nodes; and
・arrive at consensus on a datum value.

The software walkthrough has been demonstrates this process as follows:
・Each validator node polls the external FX source and stores the resulting data in its local cache.
・A proposing node constructs a statement from its locally received source data.
・Each receiving node independently validates the proposal against its own locally received data, including feed identity, timestamp, freshness, and permitted value deviation.
・A node only issues a signed endorsement when those checks succeed.
・The proof-of-concept records the statement as agreed when the configured two-of-three endorsement threshold is reached.

List of challenge KPIs and how the project addressed them
The Fund 12 Cardano Use Cases: Concept category was intended to support early-stage ideas through design research, proof of concept, and basic prototyping. Projects were expected to generate and test ideas that create utility for Cardano, use the minimum level of functionality required to obtain meaningful research and design feedback, and establish a pathway toward more substantial future technical development and feasibility testing.
1. Conduct design research addressing a potential Cardano use case — Achieved
The project produced A Comparative Analysis of Consensus Protocols used in Blockchain Networks. The research established preliminary EchoNet requirements including efficient participant communication, independent validity checking, consensus among network participants, low latency, throughput, and tolerance of malicious or incompetent validators. It evaluated a range of Cardano-native and broader distributed-consensus approaches including Hydra, Hydrozoa, Iagon, Lodestar, Midgard, NEM, Raft, Snowball/Avalanche, CometBFT, and VeChainThor.
